name: Pritzker Architecture Prize
watch: Tom Pritzker runs the Hyatt Foundation, which is behind the Pritzker Architecture Prize. Unredacted DOJ files show frequent contact with Epstein after his 2008 plea deal.
why_flagged: Founded in 1979 and sponsored by the Pritzker family's Hyatt Foundation. The laureate receives $100,000. No outside sponsors are listed.
records_note: The prize site names only its sponsor, the Hyatt Foundation, whose Form 990-PF filings for 2001 to 2024 are on ProPublica; no reports or board.
other_findings: Epstein link · Thomas Pritzker · documented: Pritzker said he "exercised terrible judgment in maintaining contact" with Epstein and Maxwell, and he denies Virginia Giuffre's allegation against him in her 2016 deposition. Pritzker retired as Hyatt executive chairman in February 2026 but kept his role at the prize foundation. Archinect reported on 24 February 2026 that the prize would delay its 2026 announcement.

name: NYU Tisch School of the Arts
watch: Steve Tisch sits on the Dean's Council of NYU Tisch School of the Arts, named after a 1982 donation from his father and uncle. DOJ files show emails from 2013 to 2017 in which Epstein described women to him, including an April 2013 thread titled "Ukrainian Girl".
why_flagged: Part of NYU, named for a 1982 gift from Laurence and Preston Robert Tisch. Its giving page names Google, the Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation and the HFPA Charitable Trust.
records_note: No records of its own: parent NYU posts financial reports and audited statements for 2007 to 2025; Tisch names three donors and 38 council members.
other_findings: Epstein link · Steve Tisch · documented: Todd Meister introduced Tisch to Epstein in April 2013, and Tisch says the emails were about "adult women", movies, philanthropy and investments, that he never went to the island, and that he deeply regrets the association. NYU did not respond to requests for comment.

name: Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra
watch: Peter Mahler sat on the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra's 35-member board until February 2026. FOX6 first reported his Epstein link on 9 February 2026.
why_flagged: FY2025 revenue $19.8M. 2024-25 report: United Performing Arts Fund $1M+; Bradley, Argosy and Laskin foundations $250,000+; We Energies Foundation, Rockwell Automation and Herzfeld Foundation $100,000+.
records_note: It posts its 2024-25 annual report with a named donor list, audited statements for 2025, a 2024 Form 990, and 31 named directors.
other_findings: Epstein link · Peter Mahler · documented: The Epstein files show Mahler worked as a recruiter for Epstein in 2013, when Epstein was looking for an assistant, and Mahler calls the allegations against Epstein "abhorrent". Mahler resigned from the board. On 13 February 2026 the orchestra said it had accepted his resignation and that the matter was unrelated to his board service.
